name: route_optimization
description:
Turn an access_path_diag verdict into one concrete routing action. The graph
owns the decision order: fix the DNS policy first (it picks the edge), then
the direct rule (it picks the path), and only escalate when both are already
in place and the path is still slow.
Inputs (filled by the harness from the diagnosis):
- ev_fault      "none" / "dns_split" / "overseas_edge" / "proxy_rule" /
"path_quality" (the access_path_diag label, lowercased)
- ev_dns_policy "present" / "absent" -- is the domain pinned to a domestic
resolver (nameserver-policy / fake-ip excluded)?
- ev_rule       "present" / "absent" -- is there already a DIRECT rule for
the domain in the proxy config?
Emitted labels (the optimization advice, in fix order):
KEEP_AS_IS        -- nothing to do.
PIN_DOMESTIC_DNS  -- pin the domain to a domestic resolver (223.5.5.5 /
119.29.29.29), exclude it from fake-ip.
ADD_DIRECT_RULE   -- add the domain to the DIRECT rule set (bypass proxy).
ESCALATE_UPSTREAM -- DNS and DIRECT are already right; the remaining
slowness is link/upstream quality, escalate.
Reference advice for the Feishu case (measured 2026-10-24):
domains   feishu.cn, feishucdn.com, bytedns1.com, cdnbuild.net,
cdngslb.com, queniurc.com, larksuite.com
dns       223.5.5.5 / 223.6.6.6 (AliDNS), 119.29.29.29 (DNSPod)
verify    re-run access_path_diag: dns_split -> consistent, edge -> domestic,
rtt -> fast (TTFB < 500ms)

fault_kind.instructions: What did access_path_diag conclude for this domain? none = healthy; dns_split = :53 differs from DoH; overseas_edge = domestic service served from an overseas edge; proxy_rule = a domestic domain is proxied; path_quality = clean path but RTT over budget.

criteria.none: The path is healthy; no optimization needed.
criteria.dns_split: The system resolver and DoH disagree.
criteria.overseas_edge: The resolved CDN edge is outside mainland China.
criteria.proxy_rule: The domain's traffic goes through a proxy.
criteria.path_quality: DNS and path are clean but RTT exceeds budget.

dns_policy_state.instructions: Is this domain already pinned to a domestic resolver (nameserver-policy / DNS split), and excluded from fake-ip? Pinning DNS first is what makes the edge domestic; a direct rule alone cannot fix a foreign edge.

criteria.present: The domain already resolves through a domestic resolver.
criteria.absent: The domain still resolves through the proxy DNS / fake-ip.

rule_present.instructions: Is there already a DIRECT rule for this domain in the proxy config? With DNS pinned, a DIRECT rule removes the proxy hop; with everything already in place, the remaining slowness is upstream/link quality.

criteria.present: A DIRECT rule for the domain already exists.
criteria.absent: The domain has no DIRECT rule and may still be proxied.
